title: Discharge Summary
key_sentences: Mrs Marsh-Okafor presented with four days of productive cough, fever and increasing breathlessness.
On arrival she was hypoxic, with oxygen saturations of 88% on room air, and a chest radiograph showed right lower lobe consolidation.
She was treated with intravenous co-amoxiclav and oral clarithromycin, and the antibiotics were switched to tablets on day four.
Her kidney function worsened on admission and recovered with intravenous fluids and the temporary withholding of ramipril.
Supplementary oxygen was weaned off by day five, and she walked independently on the ward before discharge.
The patient and her daughter were given a copy of this summary and had the opportunity to ask questions.

rows: Dr H. Lindqvist, Ashcombe Health Centre

list_items.text: Repeat kidney function blood test at the GP surgery within 7 days.
GP to restart ramipril if creatinine is below 100 µmol/L.
Chest X-ray in 6 weeks to confirm that the consolidation has resolved.
Complete the full course of antibiotics.
Drink at least 1.5 litres of fluid a day unless advised otherwise.
Return to hospital if breathlessness worsens or the fever comes back.
